title: RT-DETR vs YOLOv9: full benchmark comparison
dek: YOLOv9 beats RT-DETR at matched compute, averaging 4.0 mAP points higher and running 7.2% faster on an RTX 5070 Ti.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: At matched compute on an RTX 5070 Ti, YOLOv9 leads RT-DETR on both axes. It averages 4.0 mAP points higher across 4 nearest-parameter pairs and wins all 4, and it runs 7.2% faster on average in PyTorch. RT-DETR's advantage here is range, not results: it fields more variants, but none of its matched pairs beats YOLOv9.
RT-DETR fields 7 measured variants; YOLOv9 fields 4. Both run the same COCO val2017 protocol at 640 px on an RTX 5070 Ti, so the two ladders align by parameter count.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017. Every RT-DETR and YOLOv9 variant highlighted against the full set.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent. Each RT-DETR model is paired with the nearest YOLOv9 model by parameter count. YOLOv9 wins all 4 pairs and averages 4.0 mAP points higher. The pattern holds through the mid range: YOLOv9-M reaches 56.1 mAP against RT-DETR-R18 at 49.8 in the same parameter class.
YOLOv9 is also faster at matched compute: 7.2% faster on average in PyTorch FP32. RT-DETR's throughput lead shows up only against models in a different size class, not at matched parameters.

items.v: Both families ship under permissive licenses

blocks.text: Pick YOLOv9 across the measured range: it is more accurate at every matched pair and faster on average. Pick RT-DETR only when you need a size YOLOv9 does not field, since it offers 7 variants to YOLOv9's 4. Both ship under permissive licenses, so licensing does not force the call. See the per-variant specs on the RT-DETR and YOLOv9 model pages.
